Je m'en occupe = I'll handle it. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to take care of'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 's'occupé').

examples.trans: I'll take care of the coffee.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'solution, answer'.

examples.text: Une solution? Une grande actrice de quatre-vingts ans, libre dans trois semaines?
examples.trans: A solution? A great eighty-year-old actress, free in three weeks?

meanings.note: Toutes sortes de = all kinds of. Feminine noun ('la sorte', plural 'les sortes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kind'.

meanings.en: faire en sorte que + subjunctive = to make sure that, to see to it that
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la sorte', plural 'les sortes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'kind'.

examples.text: Tu peux faire en sorte qu'elle refuse.
examples.trans: You can make sure that she refuses.

examples.text: Si. Tu peux faire en sorte qu'elle refuse.
examples.trans: Yes, you can. You can make sure that she refuses.

meanings.note: casual object pronoun, before the verb

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne sais pas. Je voulais te faire la surprise.
examples.trans: I don't know. I wanted to surprise you.

meanings.note: Not permanent. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'temporary'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Un arrangement temporaire, juste une façade.
examples.trans: A temporary arrangement, just a facade.

meanings.note: Informal, one owner; ton, ta, tes. Spoken French det expression meaning 'your', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Tes premières vacances en huit ans!
examples.trans: Your first holiday in eight years!

meanings.note: Tout le monde = everybody. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

meanings.en: tout ce que = all that, everything that
meanings.note: Pronoun use. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: C'est tout ce que je peux faire.
Désolé, c'est tout ce que je peux faire.
examples.trans: Sorry, that's all I can do.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: travailler à Paris, travailler le dimanche

examples.text: Cannes? Tu as travaillé au festival?
examples.trans: Cannes? Did you work at the festival?

meanings.note: Spoken French num expression meaning 'thirty', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Mais il veut quelqu'un de moins de trente ans.
examples.trans: But he wants someone under thirty.

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something
meanings.note: In context. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to find'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'trouvé').

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Trouve quelque chose.
examples.trans: I don't know. Think of something.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'very'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: Un type bien = a good guy. Masculine noun ('le type', plural 'les types') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'guy'.

examples.text: On sait qui est le type sur la photo?
examples.trans: Do we know who the guy in the photo is?

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: faire sa valise = to pack one's bags

examples.text: Il m'a donné trente minutes pour faire ma valise.
examples.trans: He gave me thirty minutes to pack my suitcase.

meanings.note: before the noun; vieil before a vowel: un vieil ami

examples.text: Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

examples.text: Trop vieille? C'est quoi le rôle, une gamine?
examples.trans: Too old? What's the part, a little girl?

voilà.gloss: there is; here's; there you go

meanings.note: To present something. Invariable French adverb meaning 'there is'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Invariable French adverb meaning 'there is'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Voilà exactement le contrat que je cherchais depuis ce matin!
examples.trans: Here is the exact contract I have been looking for since this morning!

examples.text: Nous voilà enfin arrivés devant le grand hôtel.
examples.trans: Here we are at last in front of the grand hotel.

Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
